::: {#sol-gru-lm}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
lm = make_lm()
untrained_ppl = math.exp(-lm_log_probs(lm).mean().item())
train_lm(lm, 400)
gru_ppl = math.exp(-lm_log_probs(lm).mean().item())
print(untrained_ppl, gru_ppl)
# The prose below says the GRU beats the bigram model; stop the render if not.
assert gru_ppl < bigram_ppl
```

Yes.
After training,
the network's [perplexity](#def-perplexity) on the validation text is `r sprintf("%.1f", py$gru_ppl)`,
against `r sprintf("%.1f", py$bigram_ppl)` for the [bigram model](#def-bigram-model).
Before training it was `r sprintf("%.1f", py$untrained_ppl)`,
close to the `r py$n_chars` of the uniform model.
The bigram model sees one earlier character;
the network's [hidden state](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-hidden-state) can carry information from every earlier character.

:::
